reviewed_by: Source-semantic review by the Task C capture author (2026-10-23) against Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 (view_1, retail PE32 base 0x00400000), the raw retail bytes, and the linked candidate build-clean-win32/igi1.exe sha256 8e25dcde3e2ebbbcb6c8593974d4fd34ce14cec3775e00cacfbae8b4e92ca885 rebuilt 2026-10-23T11:39:06Z.
review_basis: Binary Ninja function definition, byte-level objdump re-read of the retail image, the current candidate disassembly, and the source in engine/src/retail/core/frame_natives.cpp. This review is static; the paired runtime observation is a separate record.

arguments.meaning: the new isActive value; only the low byte selects the stored dword (movsx), while the full word reaches the optional handler and is the null-handler return

signature.return: int32_t: the optional handler result, or the unmodified argument word when the handler dword is null

candidate_semantics.note: instruction-for-instruction the same load, movsbl store, handler read, cdecl handler call and EAX fallthrough

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja identifies one analyzed function at 0x0048F140 (the catalog name FX_SmokeEmit_23 is an inherited FX-namespace misnomer; identity is the VA), definition int32_t(int32_t arg1), range 0x0048F140-0x0048F165 (37 bytes), three basic blocks. The raw retail bytes re-read with i686-w64-mingw32-objdump match the byte list recorded in observed_semantics exactly, and the candidate body at 0x0041F7C0 is the same sequence with the candidate's own stack adjustment.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: One 32-bit cdecl argument is loaded once from [esp+4] at 0x0048F140 and never re-read. Only the low byte selects the stored dword (movsx at 0x0048F144); the full word is what the handler is called with and what EAX keeps on the null-handler path. The candidate loads the same word from [esp+0xc] after its 8-byte frame adjustment at 0x0041F7C3 and applies the same movsbl. No other argument is read.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: There is no scaling, no arithmetic and no literal constant in the function. The only value transformation is sign_extend_8(argument[7:0]) through movsx, which the candidate reproduces with movsbl. The stored dword is therefore 0 or 1 for the observed 0/1 arguments, and the runtime record confirms stored_flag_value 1 for argument_bits 1 and stored_equals_sign_extended_low_byte true.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The only write is the 4-byte store at 0x0048F147 to the dword at 0x005C8BFC. That VA lies in the zero-filled tail of .data (VirtualSize 0x6FC558, SizeOfRawData 0x1A000, no file-backed bytes at that VA), so the load-time value is 0. The optional handler dword at 0x005C8C18 and its context at 0x005C8C1C are read (never written) here; their only writer is the installer 0x0048F180, which has no callers in the retail image, and the paired capture observed both null at the reviewed startup call. The candidate maps the same three objects to AppContext_IsActive (0x005E1BEC), AppContext_OptionalHandler (0x005E1BE8) and AppContext_OptionalHandlerContext (0x005E1BE4).

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: The single possible call is the indirect cdecl call at 0x0048F15F to the handler dword with (argument bits, context dword), guarded by a null test; when the handler is null the call is skipped and the stack adjustment at 0x0048F161 is the only other effect. There are no other callees, no allocation, no error reporting and no writes beyond the one store. The candidate performs the identical guarded call with the same two stack arguments and the same add esp,8 cleanup.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: There is no branch other than the handler null test and no error path. On the null-handler path EAX still holds the loaded argument word and is returned unchanged; on the non-null path EAX is the handler's return value. The candidate returns the same way (the value parameter on the null path). The runtime record confirms return_equals_argument true, return_equals_stored true and return_bits 1 for the observed startup call.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The function only moves and sign-extends a 32-bit integer flag and calls an optional handler; it contains no x87, SSE or other floating-point instruction and no floating-point state is read or written. The candidate implementation likewise performs only integer moves.

limitations: The review covers the reviewed main callsite and the null-handler path. The display window handler 0x00494F50 also calls this native on WM_ACTIVATE; those invocations are out of the reviewed scope.

A runtime-installed handler (written through 0x0048F180) changes the return value to the handler's EAX; that path was observed as a secondary invocation in a contaminated pilot run and is not claimed equivalent.
The catalog function name is a misnomer; the review deliberately relies on the address and bytes, not the name.
